html:
The Chiricahua are a band of the Apache in the borderlands of southeast Arizona, southwest New Mexico, Sonora and Chihuahua. The map shows them here from the 1500s.

Like other Apache, their ancestors were Athabaskan speakers who had come south from the far north, reaching the Southwest by about the 1400s or 1500s. They lived in small family groups, hunting, gathering agave and pinyon nuts, and raiding for food and later for horses and cattle.

The Chiricahua fought Spain, Mexico and the United States in turn. Their best known leaders were Cochise and Geronimo, whose surrender in 1886 ended the Apache wars. The fuller story of the people after that is on the page for the Chiricahua Apache.
